_comment: A scripted run for `scripts/mega-e2e.sh`: a Python fixture whose tests are
red before the change and green after it. This is the second story the mock
server can tell, and it exists because the only one it could tell was the
demo — so every other end-to-end path that needed different code to be
written had no server to run against, and therefore did not exist.
Only the roles that differ from the built-in story are named. The tester and
reviewer fall through to the built-in artifacts, which is the point: a
script states the part it is about.
The Coder's edit is anchored on a line that occurs exactly once in the
fixture, and it appends. That combination is the whole reason the mega
leg is worth running at all: an ambiguous anchor or a blank one would
silently put the function somewhere else, every artifact would still
validate, and the run would still be green.

planner.summary: Add a median() function alongside mean() in src/stats.py
planner.approach: Extend the existing statistics module with a median() that sorts a copy of the input, returns the middle element for an odd length and the mean of the two middle elements for an even length, and raises ValueError on an empty sequence.

files_to_modify.description: Add median() next to the existing mean()

acceptance_criteria: The test suite in tests/ passes
constraints: Do not sort the caller's list in place

edits.replace:
return sum(values) / len(values)


def median(values):
    """Middle value of a sequence, or the mean of the two middle values.

    Raises ValueError on an empty sequence. The input is not sorted in
    place; a copy is taken first.
    """
    ordered = sorted(values)
    n = len(ordered)
    if n == 0:
        raise ValueError("median() of an empty sequence is undefined")
    mid = n // 2
    if n % 2 == 1:
        return ordered[mid]
    return (ordered[mid - 1] + ordered[mid]) / 2

coder.implementation_notes: Added median() next to mean(). Sorts a copy so the caller's list is untouched; odd lengths return the middle element, even lengths average the two middle ones, and an empty sequence raises ValueError.
coder.spec_adherence: All five acceptance criteria are met by the new function; mean() is untouched.
